result.description:
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and motivated Systems Administrator to join our team and take ownership of the organisation's IT infrastructure. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the stability, integrity, and efficient operation of our server environments, networks, and supporting systems. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver with a strong technical background and a commitment to delivering reliable, secure, and high-performing IT services. This position suits an experienced professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and can manage both day-to-day operations and longer-term infrastructure planning.
## Key Responsibilities
- Install, configure, and maintain server hardware, operating systems, software, and associated infrastructure to ensure optimal performance and availability
- Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve server-related hardware and software malfunctions across workstations, servers, and communication infrastructure, providing timely service support to minimise disruption
- Monitor network performance and system health on an ongoing basis, identifying potential issues and making proactive adjustments to maintain service quality and reliability
- Prepare and maintain comprehensive technical documentation, including operational procedures, system logs, configuration records, and IT policies and instructions
- Assess current and future infrastructure needs by regularly surveying existing systems and recommending enhancements to server capacity, network design, and technology implementation
- Ensure computer site design and layout allows all hardware and software components to integrate and function cohesively within the broader IT environment
- Manage system security measures including user access controls, patch management, antivirus solutions, and firewall configurations to protect organisational data and assets
- Plan, implement, and test backup and disaster recovery procedures to safeguard data integrity and ensure business continuity
- Administer and support databases, virtualisation platforms, and cloud-based services as required by the organisation
- Collaborate with IT team members, vendors, and internal stakeholders to deliver infrastructure projects and resolve escalated technical issues
- Provide guidance and technical support to end users and junior IT staff, promoting best practices and ensuring effective use of systems and tools
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
- Proven experience in a Systems Administrator or similar IT infrastructure role
- Strong working knowledge of Windows Server and/or Linux operating systems, including installation, configuration, and maintenance
- Demonstrated experience with network administration, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VPN, and firewall management
- Proficiency in virtualisation technologies such as VMware or Hyper-V
- Experience with backup and disaster recovery solutions and the ability to develop and test recovery procedures
- Sound understanding of IT security principles, including access management, patch management, and vulnerability remediation
- Ability to prepare clear technical documentation and maintain accurate system records
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose and resolve complex technical issues under pressure
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders
- Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and work both autonomously and as part of a collaborative team
## Preferred Qualifications
- Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate or equivalent cloud certification
- Experience with cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud
- Familiarity with scripting languages such as PowerShell, Bash, or Python for task automation
- ITIL Foundation certification or experience working within an ITIL-aligned service management framework
- Experience with Active Directory, Group Policy, and Microsoft 365 administration
- Knowledge of monitoring tools such as Nagios, PRTG, or SolarWinds
- Prior experience working in an enterprise or multi-site environment
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a supportive and collaborative IT team that values knowledge sharing, continuous improvement, and professional growth
- Access ongoing training, certification support, and clear pathways for career advancement within the organisation
- Enjoy a flexible working environment that promotes a healthy work-life balance, including hybrid working arrangements where applicable
- Contribute to meaningful infrastructure projects that directly impact the organisation's operations and strategic direction
- Competitive remuneration package with additional benefits, in an organisation that recognises and rewards performance
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Your Opportunity
We are seeking talented individuals to join our External Audit practise at KPMG.  We are open to full-time/part-time/casual/max-term/flexible working options.

IT External Audit
Our IT External Audit team assists our clients to meet their IT External audit requirements and timelines. We work as an integrated business and as part of a larger multi-disciplinary team. The team draws on a diverse and dedicated group of people, powerful KPMG methodologies, innovating capability and assets, and global resources to support our clients in achieving the right milestones. 

Audit & Assurance: External Audit
Our Audit teams provide value to our clients by delivering specialised quality audit and assurance services. High-quality, independent financial statement audits are essential to maintaining investor confidence. Our audit professionals are committed to the public interest, challenging assumptions, and unlocking valuable insights based on a solid understanding of an organisation’s business and industry.

How are you extraordinary?
•	You are analytically minded and enjoy applying structured thinking and analysis techniques to complex problems. 
•	You are a kind and compassionate leader with a passion for continually growing your leadership skills to get the best out of a diverse and multidisciplinary team.
•	You are a people-person with a love of sharing your Audit and Assurance insight and tailoring your communication appropriately for subject matter experts and clients who want to learn more.

Your Experience
To be considered for this opportunity, your qualifications, skills & experience could include:

IT External Audit
•	Experience in assisting clients meet their IT External audit requirements and timelines.
•	Supporting engagements in the preparation of clear and concise IT External Audit reports. 
•	Providing technical knowledge, direction, and training to engagement team members.
•	In a leadership role, manage small teams and oversee the planning and execution of IT External Audit client engagements
•	Supporting business proposals and business development activities by assisting in the identification of new target clients, building business relationships, and developing/presenting proposals/findings
•	An innovative mindset and passion for problem solving enabled through technology.

Audit & Assurance: External Audit
•	Experience leading, managing and executing advisory related engagements of high-profile clients and all aspects of audit delivery, client service and business development.
•	Providing technical knowledge, direction, and training to engagement team members.
•	Experience working across Private and Corporate clients is desired.
•	Qualifications in CA/CPA and CISA/CISM/CRISC, and strong IFRS skills, will be viewed favourably.

Please note, the salary ranges $60k - $100k+ with respect to your level of experience.
We are hiring for the following employment types: Casual, Max-Term Full-Time, Max-Term Part-Time, Permanent Full-Time & Permanent Part-Time.
We also have offices in the following locations:
•	Sydney

•	Adelaide

•	Gold Coast
•	Darwin

result.description:
Monash Health is a great place to work
Monash Health is Victoria’s largest and most comprehensive health service. For more than 170 years, Monash Health and its predecessors have provided safe, high-quality healthcare and service for people at every life stage. 
To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos: monashhealth.org/careers.
 
About Monash Doctors 
To help grow your career, there are more than 1,900 Junior and 1,700 Senior Doctors at Monash Health in over 200 medical specialties. We offer unparalleled opportunities in Victoria's largest & most clinically diverse teaching health service. 
 
About Supportive and Palliative Care  
The Supportive and Palliative Care Department of Monash Health is operationally based at McCulloch House at Clayton, and is comprised of the following:  
•	A 16-bed inpatient palliative care unit at McCulloch House and 5-bed unit at Casey Hospital.  
•	A bi-disciplinary (medical and nursing) Palliative Care Consultancy Service across 6 Monash Health Campuses  
•	Outpatient Clinical Services – OncoPain (refractory cancer pain clinic), RAPID (palliative care inreach program), Palliative Care Hospital in the Home collaboration, Supportive Care Clinic, Casey Palliative Care Clinic   
•	A multidisciplinary palliative care team   
•	Research Team (Post-doctoral Fellow, Research Assistants, PhD candidates)    
•	Volunteer program  
 
The unit has a broad research interest with a focus on translational research. It has produced academic publications in a broad range of areas of interest including refractory cancer pain, ketamine, interventional pain management, end-of-life care, rapid response team and life limiting illness, telemedicine, palliative care and oncology, novel approaches to healthcare delivery tracking, geriatric palliative care, anticipatory medication, and bereavement.  
 
About the role   
The Palliative Care Fellow will work as part of a multidisciplinary team to provide safe and effective person-centred care, provide teaching and supervision of junior medical staff and students.  
It is envisaged that the Fellow would work primarily on key unit research, education or service development projects, along side a clinical component and this can be tailored to interest areas. Our department has a number of ongoing and new research topics that may be of interest and is also open to the Fellows own research proposal. The Fellow will also be part of the Palliative Care weekend/on-call roster and assist in clinical leave cover. There will be opportunities provided to attend palliative medicine education and research meetings, and be part of the extensive Unit and Organisational Governance activities that the SPCU is involved in.  This provides an opportunity to progress and bridge the gap from Registrar to Consultant in a supported and safe environment.   
 
About You:   
To ensure your success in this role you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience and knowledge:  
 
As Fellow of the Unit, in addition to non-clinical activities will have a significant responsibility and may be required to undertake: 
•	Patient assessment and management in consultation with the treating consultant 
•	Support academic, research, education, training & supervision (both undergraduate and postgraduate) 
•	Student interaction and teaching 
•	Family member communication, feedback and liaison 
•	Extensive interaction with the other health professionals, especially, medical, nursing and allied health staff 
•	Self-management (incl. time management, accessing education/training and completing college requirements) 
•	Provide clinical leadership to the multidisciplinary treating team 
•	Demonstrate commitment towards key organisational initiatives 
•	Demonstrate compliance with all relevant Monash Health Policies and Procedures 
 
Mandatory requirements of the role:  
•	Primary medical degree (MBBS) or equivalent   
•	Completed Palliative Medicine Advanced Training requirements or due to complete in next 12 months 
•	All candidates will require Australian working rights 
•	Registration with the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency (AHPRA)  
•	Employee Working with Children's Check  
•	Current Drivers Licence 
For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Dr Fiona Runacres, Director, Supportive and Palliative Care on 0414 756 505.    
Our Culture and Values 
At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 
 
Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 
 
You’ll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 
 
We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 
 
We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards.  
 
How to Apply
Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. 
Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.
